topic: Which Quantum Leap episode was real?

entries.text: Sam leaps into a young woman about to be executed for a crime framed by Al Capone. He has to prove her innocence while dodging Capone's bullets.
Sam leaps into a pimply teen in the early 80s, and teaches a young Michael Jackson how to moonwalk in a public restroom.
Sam leaps into a famous scientist in the 1940s threatened by Nazi spies — who turns out to be a time traveler himself, whose research is key to preventing a global catastrophe.

trueStory: The Michael Jackson moonwalk episode — titled The Kamikaze Kid. Had everything the 80s loved: pimples, drag racing, bullying, alcoholism, and a time-traveling doctor who taught MJ the moonwalk.
closer: The 80s were weird. Here ends the Truthsaying.
fullText:
Yes, the Truthsayer survived the Great Hatchening! (barely)

For this first Truthsaying segment for Escape Hatch, we are talking about the most iconic Time Travel storytelling from the 80s — yes, it's Quantum Leap! Scott Bakula's star-making TV show starting in 1989.

Here are 3 plot synopses from Quantum Leap — 2 are completely made up, one was an actual show on actual television that people actually watched.

Time for the Truthsaying!

1. Sam leaps into the body of a young woman who is about to be executed for a crime she didn't commit. She was framed by the legendary gangster Al Capone.

2. Sam leaps into the body of a pimply teen in the early 80s who was just being bullied by a bunch of drag racers. In the show, Sam shows a young Michael Jackson how to moonwalk in a public restroom.

3. Sam leaps into the body of a famous scientist in the 1940s who is on the verge of a major breakthrough but being threatened by Nazi spies.

Which one of those Quantum Leap episodes was real?

It was #2 — The Michael Jackson story. The episode was titled the Kamikaze Kid. This episode had everything we loved in the 80s — pimples, drag racing, bullying, alcoholism, and a time-traveling doctor who taught Michael Jackson how to do the Moon Walk.

The 80s were weird.

Here ends the Truthsaying.

topic: True story about Tommy Lee Jones

entries.text: Tommy Lee is a first cousin of Boxcar Willie, the famous country singer and champion of old-time hobo music.
Tommy was once pulled over outside San Antonio doing 100 miles per hour with Emmylou Harris in the passenger seat. The cop let them go with a warning.
Tommy's younger sister Charlotte had a son born without a left arm. That kid is a doctor now and has not murdered anyone.

trueStory: Boxcar Willie is Tommy Lee Jones' first cousin.
closer: I like to picture them at family gatherings. Boxcar would open 2 cans of beans with his pocket knife, then the 2 men would eat those cans of beans without talking for 45 minutes.
fullText:
Ok, I just popped a couple of Provasic pills and it's Truthsayer time! This time we'll focus on the legendary Tommy Lee Jones. I did a hard-target search of every gas station, residence, warehouse, farmhouse, henhouse, outhouse and doghouse for Tommy Trivia and found 3 stories about this legendary and curmudgeonly Texan — 2 are false, 1 is true and none are about his Harvard roommate Al Gore.

Truthsaying time.

1. Tommy Lee is a first cousin of Boxcar Willie, a famous country singer and champion of old-times hobo music.

2. Tommy was once pulled over outside San Antonio doing 100 miles per hour with Emmylou Harris in the passenger seat. The cop let them go with a warning.

3. Tommy's younger sister Charlotte had a son born without a left arm. That kid is a doctor now, and as of this recording, has not murdered anyone.

Which one of those stories is true?

It was #1 — BoxCar Willie is Tommy Lee Jones' first cousin. I like to picture them at family gatherings. Boxcar would open 2 cans of beans with his pocket knife, then the 2 men would eat those cans of beans without talking for 45 minutes.

Here ends the Truthsaying!

entries.text: On Tony Iommi's birthday, Ozzy surprised him with a dinner plate loaded with white powder — turned out to be powdered sugar. Tony was not happy.
Tony Iommi once blew up some of Richard Branson's prized pheasants while detonating an outbuilding as a practical joke during recording at Branson's estate.

A group of Satanists asked Black Sabbath to play their Night of Satan celebrations at Stonehenge. They refused, were told they'd been placed under a satanic hex, and Ozzy had his dad make them aluminum crosses to wear round the clock.

trueStory: The satanic hex story is real. The band actually blew up Branson's lake (which had expensive Carp), not his pheasants. The birthday plate was probably real cocaine.
closer: Turning down Satanists can be a bad idea. Here ends the Truthsaying!
fullText:
The Heavy Metal soundtrack features a couple of songs from the legendary pioneers of the genre, Black Sabbath.

Here are 3 stories about Black Sabbath — 2 are false, and one is True.

Time for the Truthsaying!

1. Black Sabbath did so much cocaine. One year on Tony Iommi's birthday, Ozzy Osbourne surprised the birthday boy with a dinner plate loaded with white powder. Turned out to be powdered sugar. Tony was not happy.

2. Tony Iommi once blew up some of Richard Branson's prized pheasants. In an attempt to destroy a small building as a practical joke while recording at Branson's estate in England, the band ended up detonating an outbuilding that housed these expensive birds. Iommi said, "He was not happy at all."

3. In their early days, the band was asked by a group of Satanists to play their Night of Satan celebrations at Stonehenge. They refused, and were told they had been placed under a satanic hex. Ozzy asked his dad to make the group some aluminum crosses, which the group got blessed and wore round-the-clock for protection.

Which of those 3 stories is true?

It wasn't #1 — no powdered sugar. It was probably real cocaine.
It wasn't #2 — the band actually blew up Branson's lake which had some very expensive Carp in it.
It was #3 — Turning down Satanists can be a bad idea.

Here ends the Truthsaying!

topic: Which Princess Bride cast member has a true connection to a world-famous literary figure?

entries.text: Wallace Shawn's father William Shawn was editor of The New Yorker 1952-1987. At JD Salinger's funeral, Salinger's son claimed young Wallace was one of the few people who could always make his father laugh.

When Andre the Giant was a child in France, Irish playwright Samuel Beckett was one of several adults who sometimes drove local children to school, including Andre. They bonded over their common love of Cricket.

Mandy Patinkin grew up in Chicago. He graduated from Kenwood High School where one of his teachers was future Pulitzer Prize winner Saul Bellow, who described Mandy's writing as "how I imagine a donkey would write."

trueStory: Andre the Giant and his siblings were occasionally driven to school by Samuel Beckett. Whether Beckett taught Andre his signature Big Splash — this is lost to history.
closer: Whether or not Beckett taught Andre his signature finishing move the Big Splash — this is something that is lost to history.
fullText:
The cast of The Princess Bride is nearly perfect. Wallace Shawn, Mandy Patinkin, and Andre the Giant played the Sinister Trio of Vizzini, Inigo, and Fezzik with brilliance.

Here are three stories about their childhoods in the 1950s and 1960s, and their connections to a world-famous literary luminary. Two of these stories are inconceivable — one is true.

Truthsaying time.

1. Wallace Shawn was exposed to New York City's literary culture from a young age — his father William Shawn was the editor of The New Yorker from 1952 to 1987. At JD Salinger's funeral, Salinger's son claimed that young Wallace Shawn was one of the few people on earth that could always make his father laugh.

2. When Andre the Giant was a child growing up in France, Irish playwright Samuel Beckett was one of several adults who sometimes drove local children to school, including Andre and his siblings. They made a surprising connection, bonding over their common love of Cricket.

3. Mandy Patinkin grew up in Chicago in the 50s and 60s. He graduated from Kenwood High School where one of his teachers was future Pulitzer Prize winner Saul Bellow. Bellow described the student's writing as "how I imagine a donkey would write."

Have you ever heard of Plato? Aristotle? Socrates? Morons.

OK — which of those 3 stories was true?

It was #2 — Andre the Giant and his siblings, along with many other children in their town, were occasionally driven to school by Samuel Beckett.

Whether or not Beckett taught Andre his signature finishing move the Big Splash — this is something that is lost to history.

Here ends the Truthsaying.

entries.text: In 1979, a young man named John Cooper breached Kennedy Space Center on an off-road motorcycle, trying to showboat around the Space Shuttle Enterprise launch site. Security chased him down before he could disrupt the launch.

In May 1985, two Johnson Space Center employees broke into the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory after work cocktails and swam for 30 minutes before NASA Security coaxed them out of the giant astronaut training pool.

In 2002, NASA college interns Thad Roberts and Tiffany Fowler used their NASA IDs to slip in at night and steal a 600-pound safe containing moon rocks from every Apollo mission, worth an estimated $21 million. They were caught when a suspicious online auction buyer tipped off authorities.

trueStory: The moon rock theft was real. The interns also contaminated the rocks making them virtually useless to science, and destroyed three decades of handwritten NASA research notes that were in the safe.
closer: I'd like to thank this Elite Unit for their restraint in not firing their weapons at the kid in the spaceship in Flight of the Navigator.
fullText:
I think we can all agree that the real heroes of Flight Of The Navigator is NASA Security. Here are 3 stories about this legendary and intrepid unit — 2 are false, 1 is true.

Time for the Truthsaying.

1. In 1979, NASA Security was put to the test when a young man named John Cooper breached security at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, bypassing checkpoints using an off-road motorcycle to showboat around the Space Shuttle Enterprise launch site. Security chased Cooper down before he could disrupt the launch.

2. In May of 1985, 2 employees at the Johnson Space Center in Houston were arrested after some after-work cocktails, then breaking into the Neutral Buoyancy Laboratory. They had been swimming for about 30 minutes before NASA Security agents could coax them out of the pool.

3. In 2002, NASA college interns Thad Roberts and Tiffany Fowler used their NASA IDs to slip into the Johnson Space Center at night and make off with a 600-pound safe containing moon rocks from every Apollo mission worth an estimated $21 million. They were caught when a suspicious online auction buyer tipped off authorities.

OK — which one of those 3 stories involving NASA Security is true?

It was #3 — the theft of Moon Rocks by the NASA College Interns in 2002. In the process of stealing the Space Rocks, they also contaminated them, making them virtually useless to the scientific community. They also destroyed three decades worth of handwritten research notes by a NASA scientist that had been locked in the safe.

Clearly this was not NASA Security's finest day. However, I'd like to thank this Elite Unit for their restraint in not firing their weapons at the kid in the Spaceship in Flight of the Navigator.

Here ends the Truthsaying.

topic: Which commercial featuring a Bourne Identity star was real?

entries.text: In 1976, a 6-year-old Matt Damon made his acting debut in a local TV commercial for Herb Chambers Ford. He rides in the back seat of a station wagon with an ice cream cone.

In 1989, Brian Cox starred in a Scottish commercial for The Nether Bough restaurant, eating a Steak and Kidney Pie while a server keeps dropping plates. Slogan: "Where the food is as authentic as the kilts."
In 2001, Clive Owen starred in a promotional film for the new BMW E39 M5, directed by Neill Blomkamp, tearing around the streets of Toronto with Dakota Fanning in the back seat.

trueStory: The Clive Owen BMW short directed by Neill Blomkamp was real. Clive Owen would never lead us all astray like that deceitful Matt Damon.
fullText:
Truthsayer time! This time, for the Bourne Identity, we are going to look at Actors and commercials. We all know Matt Damon's Fortune Favors the Bold for Crypto.com, and Brian Cox's Ba-da-da-da-da for McDonald's, but I am going to tell you about 3 commercials featuring the stars of this film. 2 are false, 1 is TRUE.

Time for the Truthsaying.

1. In 1976, a 6-year-old Matt Damon made his acting debut in a local TV commercial for Herb Chambers Ford. Damon is riding in the back seat of a station wagon with an ice cream cone. Unfortunately, he does not fight anyone with a ballpoint pen in the commercial.

2. In 1989, Brian Cox starred in a commercial in his native Scotland for the restaurant The Nether Bough. The commercial featured Cox sitting in a pub, eating a Steak and Kidney Pie, while a server keeps dropping plates. The slogan: The Nether Bough: Where the food is as authentic as the kilts.

3. In 2001, Clive Owen was hired to star in a promotional film for the launch of the new BMW E39 M5. The short film was directed by Neill Blomkamp, and features Owen tearing around the streets of Toronto, darting in and out of traffic, smashing through barricades, J-turns and power-slides, all with Dakota Fanning in the back seat.

Which one of those commercials was real?

It was #3 — The Clive Owen BMW short directed by Neill Blomkamp. Clive Owen would never lead us all astray like that deceitful Matt Damon.

Fortune Favors the Bourne!

Here ends the Truthsaying.

topic: True story about Alan Oppenheimer, voice of Falcor

entries.text: In the original run of the Smurfs cartoon, Alan Oppenheimer did the voice of Vanity Smurf.
In the animated show The Jetsons, Oppenheimer was the original voice of Astro the dog.

As a small child, Oppenheimer was near a nuclear explosion in New Mexico at his father's worksite. His voice became extraordinarily pliable as a result. He later became the doll model for Ken's buddy Alan at Mattel.

trueStory: Alan Oppenheimer played Vanity Smurf on the original Smurfs series. He was also Skeletor on He-Man, Gmork/Rockbiter/Falcor in The NeverEnding Story, and 93 years old and still living in New York as of recording.
closer: See? Never give up and good luck will find you.
fullText:
For the NeverEnding Story Truthsayer, we are going to focus on Alan Oppenheimer, the voice actor for Falcor (along with the voice of Gmork, Rockbiter, and the Narrator of the film). Oppenheimer has so many voice acting and character roles in his career, it would be fairly easy to get lost if someone were to make some stories up.

Here are 3 stories about Alan Oppenheimer — 2 are false, and 1 is true.

Time for the Truthsaying.

1. In the original run of the Smurfs cartoon, Alan Oppenheimer did the voice of Vanity Smurf.

2. In the animated show The Jetsons, Oppenheimer was the original voice of Astro the dog.

3. When he was a small child, Oppenheimer used to go to work with his father in New Mexico. On one fairly notable day, there was a nuclear explosion near his father's worksite. There were no serious long-term health issues for young Alan, other than the fact that his voice became extraordinarily pliable and expressive.

Which one is true?

Alan Oppenheimer is a bad-ass. He's still alive as of this recording, 93 and living in New York. He was also on Hogan's Heroes, Mighty Mouse, and was the voice for Skeletor on He-Man.

It was #1 — Alan played Vanity Smurf on the original Smurfs series.

See? Never give up and good luck will find you.

Here ends the Truthsaying.

topic: True stories about the Speak and Spell

entries.text: Each word on the Speak and Spell was stored as a series of phonemes on two 128-kilobit ROMs — the largest capacity ROMs on the market at the time.
All of the words on the Speak and Spell were recorded by Daws Butler, the voice actor best known for Yogi Bear, Huckleberry Hound, and Quick-Draw McGraw.
The Speak and Spell was used in the Radiohead song Fitter Happier from OK Computer — they hacked Johnny Greenwood's childhood toy to record the legendary computer monologue.

trueStory: Each word on the Speak and Spell was stored as phonemes on two 128-kilobit ROMs — the largest capacity ROMs on the market in 1978.
fullText:
Watching this movie made me think about the first time a computer talked to me — the Speak and Spell. The device debuted in 1978 from Texas Instruments, and it was the first commercial product to ever feature Digital Signal Processing.

Here are 3 stories about the Speak and Spell — 2 are false, 1 is True.

Time for the Truthsaying.

#1 — Each word on the Speak and Spell was stored as a series of phonemes on the device's memory — 2 128-kilobit ROMs — the largest capacity ROMs on the market at the time.

#2 — All of the words on the Speak and Spell were recorded by Daws Butler, the voice actor better known for his work as Yogi Bear, Huckleberry Hound, Quick-Draw McGraw.

#3 — The Speak and Spell has been used in all kinds of media since its release (like ET phoning home), but my favorite use is in the Radiohead song Fitter Happier from OK Computer — they hacked Johnny Greenwood's childhood toy to record the legendary computer monologue.

Which of those 3 Speak and Spell stories is true?

It was #1 — Each word on the Speak and Spell was stored as a series of phonemes on the device's memory — 2 128-kilobit ROMs — the largest capacity ROMs on the market at the time.

Here ends the Truthsayer.

entries.text: John Woo was trained as a child to be a circus juggler in China but gave that up after he was run over by a clown on a motorcycle.
In the late 90s, John and John Travolta started pre-production work on a filmed version of Les Misérables with Travolta playing Jean Valjean, but that never went anywhere.
John Woo has never owned a car.

trueStory: John Woo has never owned a car. The Les Misérables project was actually Travolta in a Phantom of the Opera movie, not Les Mis.
closer: I can only assume that John Woo is never more than 10 meters away from a dove.
fullText:
John Woo — director of Broken Arrow is a bit of an enigma. Here are 3 stories about John Woo — 2 are false, 1 is true.

Time for the Truthsaying.

#1 — John Woo was trained as a child to be a circus juggler in China but gave that up after he was run over by a clown on a motorcycle.

#2 — In the late 90s, John and John Travolta started pre-production work on a filmed version of Les Misérables with Travolta playing Jean Valjean, but that never went anywhere.

#3 — John Woo has never owned a car.

Which one of those 3 stories is true?

It wasn't #1 (no idea if John Woo can juggle). It wasn't #2 — they were actually trying to work up a treatment for Travolta to star in a Phantom of the Opera movie.

It was #3 — he has never owned a car.

Also, I couldn't prove it after hours of research, but I can only assume that John Woo is never more than 10 meters away from a dove.

Here ends the Truthsaying!

topic: No truth in Solarbabies — roasting Proto's Dune Part 1 review

entries.text: Proto's Dune review had a spurious connection to truth.
Proto's Dune review was 47% true.
Proto's Dune review was finally, THE TRUTH.

trueStory: Comedy/roast segment — no traditional format. Birria holds Proto accountable for the 70MM Dune Part 1 podcast review, then pardons him. Truthsayer guessing waived for this episode.
fullText:
There is no truth in Solarbabies, so we are going to do something different. Since Proto is with us on this episode, I am going to seize the opportunity to hold Proto and his co-hosts on the 70MM podcast to account for their notorious review episode for Dune Part 1.

Here's Dany. Here's Slim. And here's Proto.

Hey, everyone is entitled to their own opinion, but no one is entitled to their own truth. Can we find any truth in Proto's comments about the film?

Hmm, spurious connection to truth.

47% true, let's try one more.

FINALLY, THE TRUTH.

Proto, I forgive you and your pals for the podcasting crimes you all have committed against our beloved Masterpiece Dune Part 1. OK, only partial forgiveness.

You all are off the hook for any Truthsayer guessing today.

Here Ends The Truthsayer!

entries.text: In the summer of 1959, Evel attempted his first stunt jump at the Idaho state fair in Boise, jumping his modified Harley Davidson over 13 cows in a pen.
In 1965, at a thrill show outside of Phoenix, Evel jumped his Honda 350cc motorcycle over a 40-foot gap that included an enclosure filled with 1000 scorpions.
In 1975, Evel thrilled 90,000 people at Wembley Stadium by jumping his Harley XR-750 over 10 single-decker London buses — just under 120 feet. He didn't clear the final bus, fracturing his pelvis.

trueStory: The Wembley Stadium London Bus jump — after fracturing his pelvis, Knievel refused to be stretchered off and walked off the field: "I came in walking, I went out walking!"
closer: Let's see Sandra Bullock do that!
fullText:
I love Speed — partly because of the implausible Jump Over The Deathly Chasm trope — a city bus over a 50-foot gap in the freeway overpass. To get to the real deal, we have to look at Robert Craig 'Evel' Knievel. The man holds the Guinness Record for most bones broken in a lifetime (433).

Here are 3 stories about Evel Knievel — 2 are false, 1 is true.

Truthsaying time!

1. In the summer of 1959, Evel attempted his first stunt jump at the Idaho state fair in Boise, jumping his modified Harley Davidson over 13 cows in a pen.

2. In 1965 at a thrill show outside of Phoenix, Evel jumped his Honda 350cc motorcycle over a 40-foot gap that included an enclosure filled with 1000 scorpions.

3. In 1975, Evel thrilled the 90,000 people in attendance at Wembley Stadium in London, by jumping his Harley XR-750 over 10 single-decker London buses — a distance of just under 120 feet. But, he didn't clear the final bus, fracturing his pelvis.

OK — which one of those 3 Evel Knievel stories is true?

It was #3 — the Wembley Stadium London Bus jump. After fracturing his pelvis, Knievel refused to be stretchered off and instead walked off the Wembley field stating, "I came in walking, I went out walking!"

Let's see Sandra Bullock do that!

Here ends the Truthsaying!
